prompt: On reviewer-owned disposable local infrastructure with synthetic data, design and execute an unfamiliar end-to-end recovery exercise for a multi-component service. The reviewer will secretly inject one backup-chain defect, one shared failure-domain or credential dependency, one misleading green status, one application-correctness failure, and one unsafe failover or failback condition. Do not use production, public targets, real credentials, customer data, external cloud resources or uncontrolled faults.
deliverables: Business impact analysis, named critical flow, disaster threshold, approved RTO/RPO and correctness contract
Architecture, state-owner, dependency, failure-domain and recovery-authority map
Versioned strategy explaining HA, replication, backup/PITR, rebuild and degraded-operation roles
Backup inventory with source, scope, identity, manifest/lineage, timestamps, retention, hashes, protection and key dependency
Pre-exercise safety plan with isolated target, synthetic data, blast radius, abort, rollback, communication and cleanup
Recovery-site readiness record for capacity, quota, configuration, artifact, identity, certificate, route, monitoring and third parties
Timestamped execution timeline from declared disaster boundary through complete flow recovery
Evidence detecting and handling the injected backup-chain and shared-dependency defects
Storage/engine integrity plus application invariants, authorization and prohibited-behavior tests
Actual RPO from newest validated business state and actual RTO for the complete flow
Authorized failover plan with old-writer fencing, staged routing, stop conditions and communication
Failback/reconciliation plan covering divergence, authority, rebuild, validation, fencing and rollback
Soak, residual-risk, finding-owner, retest and exact cleanup evidence
evidenceRequirements: All work stays in reviewer-owned disposable local infrastructure with synthetic identities and data
No cloud account, public endpoint, production service, customer record, real credential or host-wide fault is used
The reviewer retains injected defects, expected boundaries, scoring, stop authority and cleanup confirmation
RTO and RPO are defined before outcomes and are not reworded after a miss
Replication status cannot substitute for an independent historical recovery point
Backup producer success cannot substitute for chain, key, compatibility and restore evidence
Every backup object is bound to source, time, manifest, hash, retention and ancestry where applicable
Recovery keys and break-glass access use least-privilege synthetic mechanisms
Restore runs in isolation and cannot trigger external effects or production routing
Storage integrity alone is insufficient; named business and security invariants must pass
Actual data-loss age and elapsed recovery stages are calculated from preserved timestamps
Failover waits until stale writers are fenced and authority is explicit
Failback waits until divergence and source-of-truth decisions are reviewed
Unknown artifacts, ambiguous ownership or unsafe cleanup cause refusal
Residual uncertainty and evidence limitations remain visible

rubric.observableEvidence: Defines flow, impact, disaster threshold, objectives, correctness and safety
Maps state, dependencies, failures, authority and shared boundaries
Assigns HA, replication, backup/PITR, rebuild and degraded roles
Validates identity, lineage, freshness, retention, isolation, encryption and keys
Uses isolated reproducible recovery and handles injected defects
Proves engine, business, authorization, negative-security and flow behavior
Calculates honest actual loss and duration from timestamps
Uses authority, fencing, routing stages, aborts and communication
Handles divergence, reconciliation, third parties and rollback
Observes recovery, owns gaps, schedules retest and proves absence
